$comment: Sailing tuning, PRD section 4. A ship's condition slows her (shot-through sails, a hull below 30%, fewer hands than her minimum crew: crew.json shortHandedFloor); load and currents are not modelled yet. World pace is 0.7 of what it was (0.7 tiles/s per speed point) so a passing ship stays on screen long enough to deal with; days are longer to match (calendar.json), and the game cruises at 2x away from coasts and other ships. Wind multipliers are spread so each step up is clearly faster; gale damage risk is not modelled yet. A ship is drawn about four tiles long (render3d SHIP_SCALE), so her whole hull is kept off the land, not just her centre: hull marks her outline (bowTiles to bow and stern, beamTiles to either side), and no move may carry any point of it from water onto land. Within harbourTiles of a port only her centre is kept off the land, as before: a harbour is tight, and she must work close in to berth and to beat out. The outline holds only at the helm: a course or an intercept keeps off by its own look-ahead and by the sea lanes, which the outline would only slow (it grounded a course in the Tortuga channel). Turning is always free, so she can never be shut in; she turns, then sails clear. To feel out other values before tuning them, the game takes ?pace=0.4 (every ship at sea at that share of her speed, the day as much longer) and ?turn=0.5 (every ship turning that much slower, in battle too) in its URL; it plays at the playtest's defaults (apps/web main.tsx PLAYTEST) unless given ?pace=1&turn=1.

course.$comment: The course autopilot sails like a seaman. Beating, she goes about once she is corridorTiles off the line the wind makes through her mark, so her boards keep near the way instead of ranging across the sea. Running before the wind she broad-reaches and gybes, the best way down for her rig, once runCorridorTiles off (narrower: a wide board downwind carried her behind an island south of Hispaniola). In her destination's harbour with the berth upwind, where a ship can't beat in the tight water, her boats tow her in at towTilesPerSecond; leaving a harbour with her first waypoint upwind and land closing both tacks within 8 tiles (Cumaná into a west wind, at the mouth of the Gulf of Cariaco), they tow her out the same way. In her last approachTiles to a port she shortens sail, coming in at approachShare of her speed. A fight turns this off.
